_description: Governance rules for suggesting related Help Center article links inside release notes. Loaded by POST /api/release-notes/suggest-related-links. Edit these rules directly — no code change or server restart needed.
linkingRules: Link only when it helps the reader take action. Add links for setup steps, deeper how-to guidance, admin configuration, API docs, or feature reference articles. Example: a release note about Personal Settings or inbox behavior should link to the full Personal Settings article where users manage those preferences.

Use contextual links near the relevant feature. Place each link inside the specific release note section it supports, not only at the bottom. If a feature mentions Address Case, link to the Address Case article within that feature's 'How It Works' or follow-up sentence.
Avoid over-linking. Do not link every product term. Prioritize the article that answers the reader's likely next question: 'How do I use this?' or 'Where do I configure this?'
Use clear, descriptive anchor text. Prefer 'Learn more about Auto Replies' or 'Manage your Personal Settings' over 'click here'. This improves readability and accessibility.
Link to stable, published articles only. Never suggest a draft, internal, outdated, or soon-to-be-replaced article unless the release note itself is internal.

Keep related links current. Release notes often point to feature articles, previous release notes, or setup guides. Prefer links that will stay valid after launch — do not point users at beta or soon-to-be-replaced content.

Separate 'related articles' from required reading. In-line links should support required next steps for the feature. The Zendesk 'Related articles' section can include broader discovery links, such as previous release notes or adjacent feature articles.
